title: Buffers and streams
summary: Understand Buffer bytes and process a readable stream chunk by chunk to count lines.

options: A fixed-size block of raw bytes
A function that waits for events
quiz.explain: A `Buffer` holds binary data, such as the bytes of a file or a network message. Turn it into text with `buffer.toString()`.

quiz.q: What does this print? The letter e with an accent takes two bytes in UTF-8.
quiz.explain: `'héllo'` has 5 characters, but `é` needs 2 bytes, so the size is 6 bytes. Characters and bytes are not the same thing.

quiz.q: Why read a 5 GB log file as a stream instead of with readFile?
options: Streams are always faster for small files
A stream handles the file in small chunks, so memory use stays small
quiz.explain: `readFile` loads the whole file into memory. A stream hands you one **chunk** at a time, so even a huge file needs only a little memory.

quiz.q: A stream delivers the chunks 'ab\ncd' and 'e\nfg'. What is the safe way to find the lines?
options: Join all chunks into one text first (or keep the unfinished last line), then split
Only look at the first chunk
quiz.explain: A chunk can end in the middle of a line. Here the word `cde` is split across two chunks. Splitting each chunk separately would break it into `cd` and `e`.

quiz.q: Complete the loop that goes through every chunk of a readable stream.
quiz.explain: `for await (const chunk of stream)` waits for each chunk to arrive and gives it to the loop body. In a CommonJS file it must sit inside an `async` function.

exercise.task:
In `streams.js`, write and export two functions.

- `byteLength(text)` returns the size of the text in bytes (UTF-8).
- `countLines(stream)` is **async**. It receives a readable stream and resolves to the number of non-empty lines in all the data. A line can be split across two chunks. Chunks may be strings or Buffers.

Use `for await (const chunk of stream)`.
hints: Collect the text of all chunks into one string, then count the lines at the end. `String(chunk)` works for strings and Buffers.
`let text = ''; for await (const chunk of stream) { text += chunk; }` then split on `\n` and keep the lines that are not empty. `Buffer.byteLength(text)` does the first function.
